 Order

This petition under Section 397 read with Section 401 of Cr.P.C. is filed by the petitioners - accused Nos.1 to 5 to quash the proceedings in Crime No.61/2019 of Yadrami Police Station, Tq: Jewargi Dist: Kalaburagi and S.C.No.49/2021 pending on the file of Prl. District and Sessions Court at Kalaburagi, for the offences punishable under Sections 498(A), 307, 504 and 506 read with Section 149 of IPC and under Section 4 of D.P. Act, 1961.
02.

sentences.text: The summary of the charge-sheet is that the de-facto - complainant is the legally wedded wife of the accused No.1, accused No.2 is the brother-in-law, accused Nos.3 and 4 are the parents-in-law and accused No.5 is the sister-in-law.

On 24.05.2019 at about 11.0 a.m. the accused after forming an unlawful assembly with common intention came to the parental home of the de-facto - complainant and abused her in filthy language stating that without bringing dowry she is residing in her parental home, and her husband stated that he would contract NC: 2023:KHC-K:891 second marriage, if she does not bring dowry from her parental home.
At the instigation of other accused, the accused No.1 tried to kill the de-facto - complainant and also posed threat to her life.
03. The learned Sessions Judge after accepting the charge-sheet took cognizable of the above said offences and issued summons.
04. The accused filed an application before the Sessions Judge for discharge under Section 227 of Cr.P.C.
The learned Sessions Judge by impugned order, dismissed the said application, stating that there is a prima-facie case to proceed against the accused herein.
05. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners, the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent - State and the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 - de-facto complainant.

The petitioner No.1 - accused No.1 has produced the copy of the order dated 28.01.2021 passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge, at Yadgiri in M.C.No.5/2019, by which, the petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 filed by the petitioner No.1 - accused No.1 was allowed and the respondent therein and the de-facto - complainant herein was directed to join the company of the petitioner No.1 - accused No.1 to lead marital life.
During the pendecy of this petition, the FIR was lodged by the de-facto - complainant.

07. Perusal of the FIR and the charge-sheet material indicate that, except omnibus and general allegations, there is no specific allegation against the petitioners, as to how, and in what manner,
each of the accused herein have subjected the de-facto - complainant to cruelty both physically and mentally.
Further allegation against the petitioner No.1 - accused No.1 is that he tried to strangulate the neck of the de-facto - complainant and her parents came to her rescue.
Except the statement of NC: 2023:KHC-K:891 the de-facto - complainant, the statements of independent witnesses were not recorded.
The alleged incident has taken place on 24.05.2019 and the FIR was registered on 09.06.2019 without offering any proper explanation.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of A.P. vs M. Madhusudhan Rao, reported in (2008) 15 SCC 582, at Para No.30 has held as under:-
"30.

entities.text: State of A.P. vs M. Madhusudhan Rao, reported in (2008) 15 SCC 582
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Time and again, the object and importance of prompt lodging of the first information report has been highlighted.
Delay in lodging the first information report, more often than not, results in embellishment and exaggeration, which is a creature of an afterthought.

A delayed report not only gets bereft of the advantage of spontaneity, the danger of the introduction of a coloured version, an exaggerated account of the incident or a concocted story as a result of deliberations and consultations, also creeps in, casting a serious doubt on its veracity.

Therefore, it is essential that the delay in lodging the report should be satisfactorily explained."
NC: 2023:KHC-K:891 09.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar, reported in (2022) 6 SCC 599, at Para No.18 has held as under:-
"18.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar, reported in (2022) 6 SCC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of section 498A IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes,
without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute, if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.
Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them."
10. The prosecution has also not placed any material along with the charge-sheet to substantiate that the de-facto - complainant had sustained simple injuries.

The wound certificate nor the charge-sheet material NC: 2023:KHC-K:891 indicate that the de-facto - complainant sustained any injuries, in the form of mark on the neck of the de-facto - complainant, due to the alleged strangulation by the petitioner No.1 - accused No.1.
11.

The dispute between the parties arises out of marital discard, however given a criminal texture,
so as to wreak vengeances and with revengeful intent.
Hence, the continuation of the criminal proceedings, will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following;
ORDER I.
The Criminal Petition is allowed.

II. The impugned order dated 17.08.2022 passed by the Prl. Sessions Judge, at Kalaburagi in S.C.No.49/2021 on application filed under Section 227 of Cr.P.C. is hereby set-aside and consequently, application under Section 227 of Cr.P.C. is allowed.
